iterations.plan: I need to determine whether a Korean word ends with a consonant (batchim) or vowel to select the correct particle form, handling both Hangul syllables and digit-based numbers.
iterations.code:
def attach_particle(word: str, particle: str) -> str:
    # Get the last character
    last_char = word[-1]
    
    # Handle digits - convert to Sino-Korean number pronunciation
    if last_char.isdigit():
        # Map digits to their Sino-Korean pronunciations and check if they end in consonant
        digit_consonant = {
            '0': False,  # 영 (vowel ending)
            '1': False,  # 일 (vowel ending)
            '2': False,  # 이 (vowel ending)
            '3': False,  # 삼 (vowel ending)
            '4': False,  # 사 (vowel ending)
            '5': False,  # 오 (vowel ending)
            '6': False,  # 육 (consonant - ㄱ)
            '7': False,  # 칠 (consonant - ㄹ)
            '8': False,  # 팔 (consonant - ㄹ)
            '9': False,  # 구 (vowel ending)
        }
        # Actually check pronunciation: 육(ㄱ), 칠(ㄹ), 팔(ㄹ) have consonants
        digit_has_batchim = {
            '0': False,  # 영
            '1': False,  # 일
            '2': False,  # 이
            '3': False,  # 삼
            '4': False,  # 사
            '5': False,  # 오
            '6': True,   # 육 (ends in ㄱ)
            '7': True,   # 칠 (ends in ㄹ)
            '8': True,   # 팔 (ends in ㄹ)
            '9': False,  # 구
        }
        has_batchim = digit_has_batchim[last_char]
    else:
        # Handle Hangul syllables
        # Hangul syllables range: AC00-D7A3 in Unicode
        if '\uAC00' <= last_char <= '\uD7A3':
            # Calculate position in Hangul block
            code = ord(last_char) - 0xAC00
            # Each syllable is composed of: (초성 * 588) + (중성 * 28) + 종성
            # Jongseong (final consonant) is code % 28
            jongseong = code % 28
            # If jongseong is 0, there's no final consonant
            has_batchim = jongseong != 0
        else:
            # Fallback for non-Hangul characters
            has_batchim = False
    
    # Handle special case for "으로/로": ㄹ batchim is treated as no batchim
    if particle == "으로/로":
        if has_batchim:
            # Check if the last syllable ends in ㄹ (jongseong == 8)
            last_char = word[-1]
            if '\uAC00' <= last_char <= '\uD7A3':
                code = ord(last_char) - 0xAC00
                jongseong = code % 28
                if jongseong == 8:  # ㄹ
                    return word + particle.split('/')[1]  # Use "로"
        
        if has_batchim:
            return word + particle.split('/')[0]  # Use "으로"
        else:
            return word + particle.split('/')[1]  # Use "로"
    
    # Split particle and select appropriate form
    forms = particle.split('/')
    if has_batchim:
        return word + forms[0]  # consonant form (before slash)
    else:
        return word + forms[1]  # vowel form (after slash)
